evidence: "more than 820 facilities, up from 750 in the 2025 edition" (SEMI/TechSearch release, 7 Jul 2026, as distributed via AAP/Cision)

claim: TechCrunch reported at approval (May 2025) that the HCL-Foxconn Jewar unit will initially operate as an OSAT, packaging and testing chips fabricated elsewhere, with capacity of 20,000 wafers per month and 36 million units per month.
evidence: "at first, be used as a semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) facility. That means it will be focused on providing packaging and testing services for chips that have been manufactured elsewhere"; "will have a capacity of 20,000 wafers per month and can produce 36 million units monthly" (TechCrunch, 14 May 2025)

claim: Of the 10 projects in India's ISM approved-plants list (PIB, Aug 2025), Tata-PSMC Dholera is the only unambiguous silicon wafer fab; at least 7 are assembly/test units or include an ATMP line, HCL-Foxconn Jewar was reported as initially an OSAT, and CDIL Mohali is a brownfield discrete-device manufacturing expansion, so India's entry is back-end-led.
evidence: Count from the PIB approved-plants table (CLM-1067 to CLM-1071) plus the TechCrunch report on HCL-Foxconn (@c_hcl).
notes: Based on CLM-1066, CLM-1067, CLM-1068, CLM-1069, CLM-1070, CLM-1071 and @c_hcl. The 7: Micron, CG Power, TSAT, Kaynes, SiCSem (compound fab plus ATMP), 3D Glass Solutions (ATMP line), ASIP (system-in-package unit with Korea's APACT; back-end character inferred from name and partner). SiCSem is a compound-semiconductor fab with an ATMP line.
